record.paper_title: Gradings, Braidings, Representations, Paraparticles: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: Do the proposed paraparticle Hamiltonians built from a monochromatic parabosonic field and a (p + 1)-level system yield exactly solvable generalizations of the Jaynes-Cummings model? If so, can one compute their energy levels, eigenfunctions, and transition rates and compare those predictions directly with theoretical and experimental results?

evidence.quote: Using the Fock-like modules described above, we will attempt to proceed in a generalization of the above model in the study of the interaction of a monochromatic parabosonic field with a (p + 1)-level system.

In this way, we will actually construct a family of exactly solvable, quantum mechanical models, whose properties will be studied quantitatively (computation of energy levels, eigenfunctions, rates of transitions between states, etc.) and directly compared with theoretical and experimental results.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-mode parabosonic field of order $p$, generated by creation/annihilation operators $b^+, b^-$ satisfying the trilinear Green relations
$$[\{b^-,b^+\},b^\pm]=\pm 2 b^\pm,\qquad [\{b^\pm,b^\pm\},b^\pm]=0,$$
acting on the parabosonic Fock-like module $F(p)$ uniquely determined by a vacuum vector $|0\rangle$ with $b^-|0\rangle=0$ and $b^- b^+|0\rangle=p|0\rangle$ (so that for $p=1$ one recovers the ordinary bosonic Fock space). Couple this field to a $(p+1)$-level atomic system whose internal degrees of freedom are described by a finite-dimensional Fock-like module of an associated parafermionic algebra of order $p$, with raising/lowering operators $f^+, f^-$ obeying the analogous parafermionic trilinear relations.

Construct a family of paraparticle Hamiltonians of Jaynes–Cummings type, of the schematic form
$$H = \tfrac{\omega}{2}\{b^+,b^-\} + \tfrac{\Omega}{2}\{f^+,f^-\} + g\bigl(b^+ f^- + f^+ b^-\bigr),$$
on the tensor product module $F(p)\otimes V(p)$, together with reasonable variants involving the natural quadratic Casimir terms of the underlying paraparticle algebras.

Questions:
(a) Is every such Hamiltonian exactly solvable, in the sense that the full Hilbert space decomposes into finite-dimensional invariant subspaces on which $H$ can be diagonalized in closed form?
(b) For each such model, determine the energy spectrum and eigenfunctions explicitly as functions of $p$, $\omega$, $\Omega$, $g$, and compute the transition rates (Rabi-type oscillations, atomic inversion, photon statistics) between Fock-like basis states.
(c) Compare the resulting predictions with the standard ($p=1$) Jaynes–Cummings model and with available experimental data on cavity QED and trapped-ion systems.
artifact.status_search_result: The simplest case—a two-level atom in a single-mode para-Bose cavity field—has been treated as an exactly solvable deformed Jaynes–Cummings model, with explicit energy spectrum, eigenstates and Rabi-type dynamics computed (e.g., Dehghani et al., Sci. Rep. 2021; parity-deformed JCM, Sci. Rep. 2016). However, the full proposed program for arbitrary order $p$ with a $(p+1)$-level (parafermionic) system, including direct comparison with experiment, does not appear to have been carried out completely; thus the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: The Jaynes–Cummings model of a two-level atom in a single-mode para-Bose cavity field
status_evidence.snippet: Exact energy spectrum and eigenstates of the para-Bose deformed JC model are obtained for one-photon transitions.
status_evidence.claim: The two-level / para-Bose case is solved exactly, supporting partial solution of the broader program.

status_evidence.title: Parity Deformed Jaynes-Cummings Model: Robust Maximally Entangled States
status_evidence.snippet: Parity-deformed (parabosonic) JC model analyzed with exact eigenstructure and entanglement properties.
status_evidence.claim: Parabosonic deformations of JC are exactly solvable in the simplest case.

status_evidence.title: Gradings, Braidings, Representations, Paraparticles: Some Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes paraparticle generalizations of the JC model coupling a parabosonic field to a (p+1)-level system as an open program.
status_evidence.claim: The general (p+1)-level paraparticle JC program is posed as open.
